_comment: forest_bars: Map 3's start/finish barrier, the forest's answer to rock_bars. Not a gate: a stand of living saplings and young trunks grown up out of the ground across the lane. No frame, no post, no lintel, no rail, no cut end, nothing that reads as carpentry. Twenty-three stems rise out of the earth, each with a root flare of buttress roots at its foot, each leaning, bending and crossing its neighbours on its own; thin whippy shoots stand between the thick ones; eleven of the tall stems fork high up and nine side limbs arc out and tangle with neighbours; leaves sit only on a few limb ends and a few short stems, never as a hedge. Every cross-section is a 5-, 6-, 7- or 8-gon with a wobbled radius per ring, so no silhouette edge reads as a sawn plank. 10.6 x 8.5 m filling the lane's cross-section, 1.2 m through it; the stand blocks, proved by sampling 320 heights from z=0.05 to z=8.40 and measuring every clearance between strand axes in plan, radii subtracted -- none exceeds 0.38. Origin at the base centre, y=0 is the ground; the stand spans local X, thickness along local Z. Textured by lib/texel.py, not by the old per-face atlas window: one tiling sheet per material class (bark, leaf, root), taken from forest_build.py's OWN painters and seeds at texel.MPT = 0.05 m per texel, so the stand wears pixel-for-pixel the sheets the forest's ground and trunks wear and a stem shows the same grain at the same size as the trunk behind it. The atlas gave every face its own random window of a 256 px cell stretched to fit, which is why the stand read as cut off and smeared close up. Projection is mode="box", not the forest's "cyl": this prop is authored in LOCAL coordinates about its base centre and placed by the scene, so there is no ring for "cyl" to close round. GEOMETRY IS UNCHANGED BY THIS -- same 5720 triangles at the same positions, same collider; only the UVs and the split count moved, and `surfaces` went 1 -> 3 (one per class, sorted bark, leaf, root). One UV set, one contiguous mesh (components=1, duplicate seam vertices=0), no skin, no animation. What welds it into one mesh is what welds a real stand into one plant: a root plate buried below z=-0.04, never visible, that every ground stem is socketed into. ForestBarsCollision is ONE box (10.6 x 8.5 x 1.2 m in Godot's x, y, z: the stand's footprint and height), shipped as a `-boxcol` node -- no mesh in the file, one OMI_physics box on a static body -- so Godot imports it as ForestBarsCollision (StaticBody3D) / ForestBarsCollisionShape (CollisionShape3D, BoxShape3D size (10.6, 8.5, 1.2)); `surfaces` is the one drawn surface and `max_tris` counts only what is drawn.
